requirement: The `habeas-bootstrap-requirements` skill MUST direct agents to propose a distributed requirement for a cross-cutting convention instead of marking each of its sites with `{impl}`.
rationale:
The requirement has one obligation. The `habeas-bootstrap-requirements` skill MUST direct agents to propose a distributed requirement for a cross-cutting convention, instead of marking each site `{impl}`.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bootstrap_skill_proposes_distributed_requirements_for_conventions]` is marked `{test}` for this requirement. It does three things:
- It loads the bundled `SKILL.md` for `habeas-bootstrap-requirements` with `skill_md`.
- It extracts the `## Proposing requirements` section with `section`. That helper stops at the next heading of the same or higher level and ignores headings inside code fences. If the heading is missing, it fails an assertion.
- It uses `assert_text` to assert that the section contains `propose a distributed requirement instead of marking each site `{impl}``. `assert_text` panics when the phrase is absent.

I read the skill source, `assets/skills/habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md#section[Proposing requirements]`. It says: "When a convention applies on its own at many sites, such as how every validation function continues after a failed check, propose a distributed requirement instead of marking each site `{impl}`". The phrase is wrapped across lines in the source and matches the asserted text because `section` collapses the body. The assertion is scoped to the section where the guidance belongs, not the whole file. It would fail if the instruction were removed, moved, or reversed.

Related coverage: `the_bootstrap_skill_is_home_of_deriving_an_initial_requirement_set` checks only that the heading exists. That is a separate requirement and adds nothing here.

The obligation is a single documentation directive, and the test checks its core wording. I found no condition or input class the text distinguishes that goes untested. There are no acknowledgments or fixme references to assess.
